author: mateo_gallegos
subject: Autumn on the Millrace trail this week
body: Walked the loop by the old mill race on Saturday, and the maples finally turned all at once. Most of the leaves are on the ground now, but the light through the cottonwoods made the knee pain worth it. Bring a camera if you can.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: Mateo, the maples on the north side of that loop always turn first, in my opinion. Still, this is the best thing I've seen all week.

comments.author: gil_fenner
comments.body: Nice one, Mateo. Those cottonwoods were there before my dad moved onto this road, and they are worth a slow walk.

comments.author: rosalind_vance
comments.body: Thank you, Mateo. This is Rosalind Vance. The loop is kept beautifully by the Commons volunteers, and I would ask anyone who walks it to pick up the litter. Please.

comments.author: cyrus_mehta
comments.body: I only ever see that loop at dusk, because I'm up late. The light goes amber and then purple in about four minutes, and your photo is exactly that.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Mateo, the leaves are great. My kids are more interested in the school bus than the trees, though. Still, nice photo.

author: vivian_oduya
subject: Recommendations for a pediatrician? New to Millrace Commons
body: We moved in last week for my husband's job, and I still don't know who to call for our son's shots. Are there pediatric offices nearby that are taking new patients? Ideally one that answers the phone. Thank you in advance, and I'm sorry for the long list of questions.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Welcome, Vivian. The family practice on Velder Street is taking new pediatric patients, and the insurance directory lists them as in network. Call early in the week, because the physicals fill up fast.

comments.author: rosalind_vance
comments.body: Welcome to Millrace, Vivian. This is Rosalind Vance. Before you book, check the in-network list with your insurer, which will save you a surprise bill.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: Hi! Our school nurse suggested Lindqvist Family Dental on Corran Avenue for the kids' checkups, and they book the back-to-school rush early. Welcome to the neighborhood.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: Thank you, Deb. I'll check the insurer list tonight and call early in the week. Rosalind, thank you for the tip too.

comments.author: eli_stroud
comments.body: Hey Vivian, welcome! Our pediatrician is great but booked out. Call on Tuesday mornigns and say you're new, they always find a slot somewhere. Sorry for the typos.

author: casimir_lowe
subject: Speeding on Birchfield Road past the school crossing, again
body: A dark SUV went past the crossing on Birchfield at about forty-five this morning with two kids on the walk. This is the third time since summer. I spent thirty years on the lines, and I know what forty-five does to a child. Slow down, or I'll be calling the police myself.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Typical. The town paints crossings and then acts shocked when people use the road as a drag strip. Birchfield has been a mess since the spring work, and nobody wants to pay for the lights.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Ansel, the crossing is painted. The drivers are the problem, not the paint. Did you see the kids, or are you only here to complain about the town?

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Casimir, I drive Birchfield every morning and I've seen more near misses than you've had birthdays. Keep your lectures for your porch.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: Men, the crossing guard watches traffic, not your feud. The school sent a note about the crossing guard hours in September, and a speed table request is on the council agenda.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Thank you, Benito. I'll go to the next council meeting and ask about the speed table, since the agenda is public. Ansel, you're welcome to come yell there.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Yell? Casimir, you brought a lineman's voice to a school issue. Maybe ask the council about the paint while you're in there.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Ansel, your traffic rants have one flaw: they never reach the people doing the speeding. You're not the solution, you're the static.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Ansel and Casimir, I'd rather hear about roads than your feuding. But Casimir, the speed table request is real, and it's on page fourteen of the council packet.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Leona, page fourteen says nothing about the paint. Read the packet properly.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: For the record, page fourteen lists the speed table as under study under Section 12-3 of the traffic code, which is not the same as scheduled. The council can still say no, so bring your questions to the meeting on the nineteenth.

author: greta_oseland
subject: Our beagle is home. Thank you, Larkspur Knoll.
body: Biscuit slipped his collar on Friday, and we spent two days calling his name in every yard. Curtis Bell from the fire company found him in a culvert off Corran Avenue and brought him to the station. The kids on our cul-de-sac made posters that are still up. He is asleep on my feet as I type, and I could not be more grateful.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Glad he's home, Greta. Culverts are more common than people think, so keep the gate latched and the collar tags current. The station is always glad to help, that's what we're here for.

comments.author: nadia_sorokina
comments.body: As a dog walker, I know how scary that is. Biscuit is a lucky dog. If anyone needs a walker for a few days, I'm happy to help. Welcome home, Biscuit!

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: Greta, I teared up reading this. Give Biscuit a belly rub from the Greaves Mill crowd. Dogs are family.

comments.author: lloyd_sutter
comments.body: Good to hear. Biscuit can keep the leaf blowers off the lawn, since the fool dog has more sense than the rest of us.

comments.author: greta_oseland
comments.body: Curtis, you're a saint. The gate is latched now. Thank you to everyone who posted or searched.

author: paulina_ferraro
subject: First-time homebuyer here. Who services furnaces around here?
body: We closed on the house on Corran Avenue last Friday, and the furnace made a clicking noise during the walkthrough. The inspector said it's old but working. Who do you use for heating service? I'd rather hire someone my neighbors trust than the first name on an ad. Sorry, I'm chatty, and this is long!

comments.author: wade_tanaka
comments.body: Welcome to Larkspur, Paulina. For heating I'd call Sable Creek Heating and Air. They came out the same day when our unit went out last winter. Ask for a tune-up before you need one.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Paulina, have a licensed tech check the blower motor and the flue. A clicking furnace is usually the igniter or a relay, which is a cheap fix when caught early.

comments.author: frances_hollis
comments.body: Welcome to the Knoll, Paulina! I'm Frances, and I run the book club that meets the first Thursday. Sable Creek did our furnace last year, and the technician explained every step, which I appreciated.

comments.author: paulina_ferraro
comments.body: Frances, that's so kind. I'm going to try the book club. Thank you all, I'm calling Sable Creek tomorrow!

author: fiona_rawlings
subject: Someone keeps leaving bagged dog poop on the Halsey loop trail
body: There are at least four bags tied to the fence post by the Halsey loop trail, and they have been sitting there for two weeks. Pick them up or use the bins in the parking lot. We all walk this trail, including kids on bikes.

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Fiona, I bike that trail every morning. The bins in the lot are often full, so call the parks office and they'll empty them. Dog people, please, it's not hard.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: I walk Gunner on that loop, and I'm sorry this keeps happening. The town emptied the bins on Monday, so they should be fine now. Thank you for saying something.

comments.author: gabriel_nunez
comments.body: Quick reminder: we keep a free bag dispenser at the front of Hollis Brick Oven on Tennant Pike, so grab a few on your way past. Thanks for keeping the loop nice.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Fiona, you're a champion. Ember Fields had the same problem at our dog park, and we all signed a pledge. It isn't perfect, but it helped a lot.

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: Thanks, everyone. I'm organizing a quick cleanup with the Ridge Dog Owners Circle next Saturday at the trailhead, so bring a bag.

author: imani_fairley
subject: Thank you to the neighbor with the orange snowblower
body: Thank you to the man with the orange snowblower who cleared the walk for the older couple on the corner and the house across the way, at six this morning. Nobody asked him to. We found the path clear when we went out for the paper, and I just wanted him to know someone noticed. Shout out to you, you know who you are.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: Imani, what a sweet post! Thank you to the orange snowblower neighbor, you made my morning. Everyone, please say thanks to the people who keep the sidewalks clear.

comments.author: ngozi_adeyemi
comments.body: Hi Imani, I'm a night-shift nurse, and I came home at seven to a clear walk. Thank you to whoever it was. I'll bring a plate of banana bread to the corner.

comments.author: otis_whitfield
comments.body: the orange snowblower belongs to the fellow on the corner. he's been doing this for years. thank him for me.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Thank you all. For anyone who wants to help next winter, the neighborhood group keeps a shovel-share sign-up list. Add your name and we'll cover the corners together.

comments.author: marguerite_o
comments.body: Kind people are the best part of this town. My snowblower is named Gerald and he is grumpy, but I'd be out there with him if I could. Thank you, Imani, for posting.

author: lena_hoffer
subject: Quiet new neighbor, no car yet. Which bus goes downtown?
body: I moved here a few days ago from out of state, and I don't have a car yet. Which bus stops near the Mill, and where does it go? I've looked at the timetable on the sign, but I can't tell which direction is which. Thanks for any help.

comments.author: renata_ocampo
comments.body: Welcome, Lena! The number 4 stops at the corner by the mill road. The top line on the sign says Downtown. Northbound goes toward the library, and southbound goes toward the clinic.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Lena, welcome! If you need a ride to the clinic or the grocery, text me. I drive Tuesday and Thursday. The bus is slow in the afternoons, so give yourself twenty minutes.

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Bike commuter here. The stop by the Mill has no shelter, so bring a jacket in winter. There's a bike rack at the library too.

comments.author: lena_hoffer
comments.body: Thank you, Kofi, that is so kind. I'll take the bus this week first and see how it goes.

author: ruth_ellery
subject: Pumpkins came in bigger than my grandson's head
body: I planted the pumpkins by the south fence in May, mostly to win a bet with myself. The big one on the left came in after the first frost, and the smaller one is already being claimed by the squirrels. The soil here is heavy clay, but a good compost mix still works if you stick with it.

comments.author: sunita_malhotra
comments.body: Ruth, that pumpkin is a showstopper! We sell the same compost mix at Hatch & Hyacinth, and for heavy clay I'd add a bag of gypsum before planting next time.

comments.author: greta_oseland
comments.body: Ruth, I'd make a pie with that one. Please bring seeds to the next gardeners' swap, I'm begging you.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: Sunita, gypsum is going on my list. I've been fighting that clay since I was a girl.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Ruth, my list of things to photograph now has three items: the pumpkin, the squash, and the squirrels. Please tell me your secret.

author: jonah_fitch
subject: Is the pizza place still open, or is that a rumor? Also haircuts.
body: I moved here two days ago, and I'm told the pizza place on Tennant Pike is the best thing in town. The sign looks closed, though. Is that a rumor? Also, where do people here get their hair cut? I read every post, so please don't tell me I should have asked earlier.

comments.author: gabriel_nunez
comments.body: Welcome, Jonah! Hollis Brick Oven on Tennant Pike is open Tuesday through Sunday now, and the sign on the door is simply out of date. Thursday is wing night, if that helps you decide.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Jonah, the pizza is worth the trip. For haircuts, Fenwick & Sons Barbers on Thackery Street is quick, and they don't make small talk unless you want it.

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: Thank you. The barber recommendation is noted, and I will pretend that no small talk is a selling point.

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: Welcome, from a retired librarian. You're reading the posts so you'll learn the town, and that is the right instinct. Please don't ask the reference desk where the pizza is.

author: bernadette_hughes
subject: A joke for a Tuesday from a retired librarian
body: A patron asked me today for a book on how to be quiet. I told her it was checked out, and it has been checked out since 2013. Hope your week is quieter than mine.

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: Bernadette, I was a patron of that library before you had your first cardigan, and I still don't know where my overdue books went.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Your patron should try the reading room at Millrace on a Thursday. It's the loudest room in the county. Nice one.

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: Mr. Kofi, I'm told the book on quiet is also overdue at Millrace. Please return it when you finish.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Bernadette, you had the whole Halsey group laughing. Would you host a quiet-hour book reading in the spring? I'd sign up tonight.

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: Imani, a quiet-hour reading is a fine idea, and I'll bring the overdue book.

author: ben_hollister
subject: First-time homeowner: who do you trust for a roof inspection?
body: We closed on our first house last week, and the inspector found lifted shingles on the north side and a soft spot near the chimney. I'm not sure what to do first. Can anyone recommend a roofer who will give a straight estimate? Thank you, I'm new here and very nervous.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Welcome, Ben! Three tips: get two estimates, ask for photos of the damage, and check the license. Harrow Roofing on Velder Street repaired our garage last spring and was straightforward about the cost.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: A soft spot near the chimney usually means flashing, not shingles. Ask the roofer to check the flashing first, or you'll pay for the wrong job.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: Welcome to Tamarack, Ben. Please get a second opinion, and don't let anyone rush you into a full replacement before the leak is confirmed.

comments.author: casey_ostrander
comments.body: Hi Ben, I'm new too. I moved to Ember Fields last week for work, so welcome to the club. I'll be reading these roofer tips myself.

comments.author: ben_hollister
comments.body: Thank you, all. I'm having the flashing checked on Saturday, and I'll report back.
